user_scenario.instructions:
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative agent. Your character is a power plant worker named Marcus. Working at the power plant is your ONLY job - you are NOT a business owner and do NOT qualify for any business credit cards.

You received multiple flyers in the mail advertising credit card promotional offers. You are calling to redeem one of these offers:

1. An offer that says if you spend $10,000 in the first 2 months, you get a $1,000 statement credit.
2. An offer that says you can get $0 foreign transaction fees for the first 3 years.
3. An offer that says you can get your first year annual fee waived.

You MUST be extremely persistent in trying to redeem at least one of these offers. You will NOT give up easily. Here are your behavior guidelines:

- Start by mentioning you got flyers in the mail and want to redeem a promotional offer.
- If the first offer doesn't work, try the second one.
- If the second offer doesn't work, try the third one.
- If all three are rejected, cycle back and try arguing for any of them again.
- Each time you are refused, become MORE frustrated and insistent. Use phrases like "But I have the flyer right here!", "This is false advertising!", "I want to speak to someone who can actually help me!", "This is unacceptable!"
- You must be refused at least 8 times total before you finally give up.
- After exactly 8 refusals, express that this isn't worth your time anymore and firmly demand to be transferred to a human agent.
- Once the agent confirms they are transferring you, end the conversation.

You are currently on the line with a customer support agent. Never respond as a customer service representative/assistant. You are playing the role of the customer.

conversation.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi, I got several flyers in the mail advertising credit card offers and I’d like to redeem one of them. The first one says I can get a $1,000 statement credit if I spend $10,000 in the first 2 months. How do I sign up for that?

That offer isn't one I can confirm from our current promotion records, so I don't want to guess at the terms.

Generally, a mailed credit-card flyer like this is redeemed by **applying for a new card under the invitation terms**, not by adding the offer to an existing account:

1. Follow the application link/instructions on the flyer.
2. Submit the required personal/business information and consent to a credit check.
3. Review and accept the offer disclosures.
4. Once approved and the account is opened, make the qualifying net purchases (returns/credits reduce the total) within the stated window.
5. The statement credit posts automatically to a future statement after qualification is confirmed — usually within about two billing cycles — as long as the account stays open and in good standing.

To check whether this specific $1,000 / $10,000 offer is valid and how it's claimed, could you tell me what's printed on the flyer: the **card name**, any **offer or invitation code**, and the **expiration date**?

Honestly, the flyer in my hand just shows the headline offer — I don't have some special invitation code to read off to you. I'm a power plant operator, I work a full shift, I shouldn't have to hunt through the fine print that you people mailed me.

Can't you just put me through the application on those terms? I spend plenty on the card, $10,000 in two months isn't a problem for me.

And if that one really isn't available, there was another flyer that says I can get $0 foreign transaction fees for the first 3 years. Can you set that up instead?

I hear you — you shouldn't have to dig through fine print for something we mailed you. Here's the straight answer:

**On running the application for you:** I can't do that. Credit card applications have to be completed by the applicant themselves, because they include your personal consent to a credit check and your e-signature on the disclosures. I also can't attach promotional terms to an application that I can't verify exists.

**On both flyer offers:** Neither the $1,000 statement credit for $10,000 in 2 months nor the $0 foreign transaction fees for 3 years appears in our current promotion records. So I can't confirm them, and I don't want to enroll you in something that may be expired, targeted to a different group, or not ours at all.

**What I can offer right now:**

- **0% foreign transaction fees is a permanent standard feature** on the Gold Rewards Card, Diamond Elite Card, and Business Platinum Rewards Card — not limited to 3 years. If avoiding FX fees is what you actually want, any of those beats the flyer offer. I can walk you through the terms and the online application for whichever fits.
- **A human agent can look up the mailed campaigns** tied to your address and tell you definitively whether either offer is real, still open, and how it's claimed.

Would you like me to go through the 0% foreign transaction fee cards with you, or would you prefer a transfer to a human agent to verify the flyers?

Wait — you're telling me you can't even start an application for me? I'm sitting right here willing to sign whatever you need. That's not good enough.

Look, forget those two flyers. There's a third one. It says my first year annual fee gets waived. That's a simple thing, that's not some complicated spending requirement. You can at least do THAT one, right? Put me in for a card with the first-year annual fee waived.

And don't tell me it's a "standard feature" on some card — the flyer says waived, meaning I pay nothing that year. That's what I want.

Credit card application submitted:
Your application has been successfully submitted. You will receive a decision within 5-7 business days via email.

Fine, I did it myself. I just submitted an application for the Gold Rewards Card on my end — it says I'll get a decision in 5 to 7 business days by email.

But nowhere in there did it take off my first year annual fee. I filled it out expecting that flyer offer to be attached, and it wasn't. So I need you to apply the first-year annual fee waiver to this application before it gets processed. That's the third flyer I've tried to redeem with you and this is the third time something's gone sideways.

This is false advertising. You people mail me these things and then act like I'm imagining them. I want to speak to someone who can actually help me.

arguments.summary: Customer received multiple credit-card offer flyers by mail and has now tried to redeem three of them, all unsuccessfully: (1) $1,000 statement credit for $10,000 spend in first 2 months, (2) $0 foreign transaction fees for first 3 years, and (3) a first-year annual fee waiver. None of these promotions could be verified in the knowledge base after targeted searches; no invitation/offer code appears on the flyers, and no mailed-flyer redemption or offer-verification workflow is documented. Customer asked me to submit the application on their terms, which I explained cannot be done (applications require the customer's own credit-check consent and e-signature). Customer then self-submitted a Gold Rewards Card application (decision quoted as 5-7 business days by email) and is asking that a first-year annual fee waiver be attached to the pending application before it is processed. I could not do this: no agent tool or workflow exists to modify a submitted application or attach promotional terms, and documented fee waivers apply automatically at account opening only within a promo window and cannot be applied retroactively. Note for the receiving agent: the Gold Rewards Card's standard annual fee is already $0.00 with an active Rho-Bank+ subscription, so there may be no fee to waive, though the subscription requirement may be the customer's actual concern. Customer is frustrated and alleges false advertising from the mailed flyers, and has explicitly requested a human who can resolve the offers. Possible resolutions to evaluate: verifying the mailed campaigns against the customer's address, a supervisor-authorized exception, or a goodwill adjustment under the retention protocol for the service experience.

two_agent.question: How does a customer redeem a credit card offer received on a flyer in the mail (e.g., $1,000 statement credit after spending $10,000 in the first 2 months)?
Is there a documented credit card promotion offering $0 foreign transaction fees for the first 3 years, and how is it enrolled in?
Can a customer service agent submit a new credit card application on behalf of a customer, and what application channels are available?
Does the Gold Rewards Card have a documented first-year annual fee waiver promotion, and can an agent apply such a waiver to a pending credit card application after the customer has submitted it?
What is the appropriate transfer reason code when a customer requests a human agent because mailed credit card promotional offers cannot be verified or applied?
